question_text:
A motorist has had too much alcohol to drink and therefore must not drive. How is it not possible for him to recover his ability to drive in a short time?
By

options.text: - drinking two cups of strong coffee
- going for a walk for half an hour

correct_answers.text: - drinking two cups of strong coffee
- going for a walk for half an hour

comment: After heavy consumption of alcohol, there's no quick way to restore your ability to drive. Neither sleeping nor walking is enough. The alcohol concentration in the blood also does not change by drinking strong coffee. The body breaks down only about 0.1 permille alcohol per hour.

question_text: Which substances can impair fitness to drive in a similar way to alcohol?
comment: Drugs, in particular, change perceptions and impair the ability to respond quickly and appropriately. Because of this, drug use of any kind make you unfit to drive. Even some medicines can impair your driving abilities. If you are prescribed medication by the doctor, pay attention to the instructions in the instruction leaflet.

question_text: What can impair fitness to drive?
comment: Anything that negatively affects the sense organs can reduce the ability to drive. In addition to drugs, this includes medications, so you should read the package leaflet before taking them. At a blood alcohol level of 0.3 permille, you are already unfit to drive. Fatigue is one of the most common causes of accidents. Here your attention and concentration cease, and this can lead to so-called microsleep.

question_text: In general, how long does it take before an alcohol level of 1.0 per mille (100 mg/100 ml) is cleared from the blood stream?
comment: The rule of thumb is: 0.1 permille is being broken down per hour. After 10 hours, 1.0 permille are completely degraded.

question_text: What can increase the intoxicating effect of alcohol?

options.text: Sleeping pills, pain killers or sedatives

correct_answers.text: Sleeping pills, pain killers or sedatives

comment: The effect of alcohol is enhanced by medication. Especially large amounts of alcohol in combination with sleeping pills, painkillers or tranquilizers can be life-threatening. If you drink alcohol on an empty stomach or consume a large amount of alcohol in a short period of time, the alcohol enters your blood immediately: you are suddenly dead drunk.

question_text: What can be the effects of even small quantities of alcohol?
comment: Even small amounts of alcohol affect your central nervous system and worsen your perception: your hearing and vision, your ability to react and perform, your sense of balance. Your willingness to take risks increases, dangers are no longer recognized by you. You think you are roadworthy, even if that is not true.

question_text: What effects can drugs have?

options.text: Prolonged improvement in physical and mental capabilities

comment: Drug substances affect the central nervous system and distort sensory perception. Although you will feel more efficient under the influence of drugs, your real performance will be reduced and makes you unable to drive. Compared to other intoxicants, drugs are more addictive.

question_text: Which drugs can make a person temporarily unfit to drive even when consumed on a single occasion?
comment: The use of drugs even in small quantities leads to temporary inability to drive. Unlike alcohol, there are no limits for drugs. Driving under the influence of drugs can mean the loss of your driver's license.

question_text: When is a drug-dependent person fit to drive a motor vehicle again?

options.text: After he/she can be shown to have stopped taking drugs for at least one year and is not likely to have a relapse
If he/she has not taken drugs for one month
If he/she has not taken drugs for six months

correct_answers.text: After he/she can be shown to have stopped taking drugs for at least one year and is not likely to have a relapse

comment: Anyone who was caught driving under the influence of drugs had to hand in his driver's license. If he is a drug addict, the person must live drug-free for a full year before he can get back his driving license. Proof of this is given by the Appraisal Body (Ger. Begutachterstelle für Fahreignung (BfF)) in form of a report.

question_text: How is the intoxicating substance in hashish broken down by the body?
comment: Drugs such as hashish are not broken down evenly in the body - in contrast to alcohol, for example. Therefore, one cannot make a reliable prediction in this regard.

question_text: What are the consequences for a person driving a motor vehicle under the influence of drugs (e.g. hashish, heroin, cocaine)?

options.text: Confiscation of driving licence or driving ban

correct_answers.text: Confiscation of driving licence or driving ban

comment: Driving a vehicle under the influence of drugs such as hashish, cocaine or heroin may result in: withdrawal of the license, a fine and/or imprisonment. Imprisonment may amount to up to five years if other persons were endangered. In order to get your driving license back, you have to undergo a medical-psychological assessment (MPA).

question_text: What are the possible effects of hashish consumption?

options.text: Intoxication with dangerous hallucination and reduced reaction capability

correct_answers.text: Intoxication with dangerous hallucination and reduced reaction capability

comment: The consumption of hashish leads to states of intoxication in which the feeling for time and space is lost. Attention is lowered, the perception of the environment is clearly obscured. There may be sensory illusions and states of confusion, as well as hallucinations.

question_text: What are the possible effects of hashish consumption?

options.text: Increased likelihood of mistakes in assimilating information

correct_answers.text: Increased likelihood of mistakes in assimilating information

comment: The use of hashish puts the user in a state of intoxication in which the ability to assess risks is lost. The feeling for time and place is lost and hallucinations as well as misperceptions can be the result. Distances and speeds can no longer be estimated correctly. The willingness to take risks as well as the tendency to misjudgments are increasing rapidly.

question_text: Who is not allowed to drink alcohol when driving motor vehicles?

options.text: All drivers during their probation period

correct_answers.text: All drivers during their probation period

comment: During the probation period or before the age of 21, a limit of 0.0 permille applies to you before each journey and while driving a motor vehicle: an absolute alcohol ban.

question_text: Are drivers during their probation period allowed to be under the influence of alcohol when driving motor vehicles?

options.text: Yes, up to a blood alcohol level of 50 milligrams if they have not committed any alcohol related traffic violation
Yes, up to a blood alcohol level of 30 milligrams if they have not committed any alcohol related traffic violation

comment: During the probationary period you must not drink any alcohol if you want to drive a motor vehicle. In general, you should stick to 0.0 permille when participating in traffic.

question_text: Why can fitness to drive be impaired even by just a small quantity of alcohol?

options.text: Because this reduces the field of vision
Because this reduces the reaction time

correct_answers.text: Because this reduces the field of vision

comment: Even small amounts of alcohol have a negative effect on vision, responsiveness and perception. The willingness for hasty actions increases and the estimation of distances as well as attention declines.

question_text: How can the consumption of cannabis products affect driving performance?

options.text: The awareness of other traffic decreases

correct_answers.text: The awareness of other traffic decreases

comment: The consumption of cannabis products is counterproductive to the ability to drive. Regardless of individually different manner of reactions and behaviors after consumption, the ability to focus on traffic generally decreases while the sensitivity to glare increases.

question_text:
Why is consuming drugs even just once, dangerous for driving on public roads?
Because it

options.text: - can result in my unfitness to drive
- can result in an intoxication state lasting for several hours

correct_answers.text: - can result in my unfitness to drive
- can result in an intoxication state lasting for several hours

comment: Drugs usually cause perceptual disorders. Even the one-time use of drugs can lead to a high lasting several hours. You as a consumer would be unfit to drive.

question_text: How long does cannabis and its degradation products remain detectable in urine?
comment: Cannabis and its breakdown products are traceable in your urine for a period between ten days and three months after consumption. The exact amount of time depends on the consumption frequency and the accuracy of the test.

question_text: Why is an individual unfit to drive after consuming the drug crystal meth?

options.text: Because of the possibility of experiencing hallucinations
Because it is possible to over-estimate personal capabilities
Because of the possible sudden onset of fatigue

correct_answers.text: Because of the possibility of experiencing hallucinations
Because it is possible to over-estimate personal capabilities
Because of the possible sudden onset of fatigue

comment: "Crystal Meth" has a negative effect on the driving ability for the following reasons: The drug causes delusions. It caters the overestimation of one's own performance and sudden exhaustion. Even the consumption of small amounts makes you unfit for driving.

question_text: How can your fitness to drive be quickly restored following the excessive consumption of alcohol?

options.text: By drinking two cups of coffee

comment: As alcohol degrades very slowly in the body, nothing can restore your driving ability in the short term.

question_text: What can affect ability to drive in a similar way to alcohol?
comment: Alcohol, drugs and medication have a negative effect on our reaction time, inhibition and motor skills.

question_text: How can the consumption of cannabis products affect the driver?

options.text: It reduces the awareness of other traffic
It reduces the ability to concentrate on driving

correct_answers.text: It reduces the awareness of other traffic
It reduces the ability to concentrate on driving

comment: After cannabis use, your perception is clouded and your ability to concentrate decreases.

question_text: What effects can result from taking drugs?
comment:
Drugs lead to noise. This also changes the perception of a person. These intoxicating states can cause various impairments, such as the impairment of the concentration and an incorrect assessment of the speed.
Furthermore, there may be an increase in the risk of risk, since it is very common to misjudge critical situations or your own driving ability.

question_text: Consuming what substance before or while driving, can make you unfit to drive?
comment:
For all drugs and substances listed here, consumption will lead to driving inability.
Drugs and alcohol at the wheel lead to a significant risk to road traffic because they significantly restrict attention and concentration. In addition, taking alcohol and drugs can have numerous physical and psychological effects, as can the misjudgments of critical situations or the overestimation of one's own driving ability.
